title: Product Detail Photos: Close-Ups of Texture | AIVideosUGC
description: Turn one sharp photo into a close-up of stitching, grain, hardware or finish. AI product detail photos for listing galleries and paid social ads.
h1: Product Detail Photos of Stitching, Grain and Finish
lead: Open a close-up scene, add one sharp photo of the feature, and download a square image filled with stitching, grain or hardware.

steps.d: Upload a steady, well-lit photo where the stitching, texture or clasp is already visible. That feature becomes the subject of the close-up.
Name one feature to enlarge and one simple setting. The result is a square image where that detail fills the frame.
Download the close-up and check color and construction against the source. Place it after the full product photo, not in its place.

faq.q: Which details should a close-up show?
faq.a: Pick one feature shoppers use to judge construction: stitching, grain, a clasp, a zipper, a rim or the finish. One close-up should answer one question.

faq.q: How close should the source photo be?
faq.a: Keep the feature sharp and leave enough of the product to show where it sits. A blurry wide shot will not become a readable macro.

faq.q: Will the close-up invent texture that was not photographed?
faq.a: It should not. If the stitch, grain or clasp is blurry or out of frame, take another photo. Compare the download with the source before you post.

faq.q: Can the close-up replace the main photo?
faq.a: No. Keep the full product first. Use the close-up after it, where shoppers inspect material or construction.

faq.q: Can I use the close-up in a carousel?
faq.a: Yes. Pair it with the full product image and a short caption about the feature. The download has no watermark.

faq.q: Do I need a macro lens?
faq.a: No. A sharp phone photo can be the source. The close-up is generated from it, and you still compare color and construction before posting.

faq.q: What does a detail photo cost?
faq.a: Each product photo costs 24 credits. The cost is shown before the job starts, and a failed job returns those credits.

faq.q: Where should the close-up sit in the gallery?
faq.a: Place it after the full product image and before lifestyle shots, so the quality question is answered while the item is still clear.

faq.q: How many detail views should one product have?
faq.a: Start with one close-up per material or construction question. Add another only when it shows a different feature.

faq.q: Does the close-up have a watermark?
faq.a: No. The download has no watermark. Check the color against the source photo before you publish.

steps_h2: How to Make Product Detail Photos in 3 Simple Steps
steps_lead: One sharp source, one named feature, then a square file that sits after the full product photo.

reviews.h2: The Feature Shoppers Check Up Close
reviews.lead: Leather goods product photos work this way. A clasp, a zipper or wood grain can too: one feature, taken from a sharp photo.

items.d: A bag shop enlarges a handle stitch so the thread and hole spacing fill the square.
A belt shop brings the leather grain forward from a sharp photo and leaves the buckle out of this frame.
A wallet shop fills the frame with a painted edge so the finish is the whole photo.
A jewelry shop enlarges a lobster clasp from a photo where the clasp was already sharp.
A shoe shop shows the welt and stitching along a sole, one construction question in one square.
A watch shop enlarges the crown and case edge, then checks them against the source before posting.
A jacket shop fills the frame with zipper teeth and tape as the texture shot on the listing.
A home shop makes a tabletop grain close-up from a photo that already showed the surface.
A hardware shop enlarges a metal knob so shoppers can judge the sheen.
An apparel shop shows a hem seam in one square and keeps the full garment photo as the first image.
